paper.title: Corrupt Bandits for Preserving Local Privacy

settings.name_in_paper: Bernoulli corrupt bandit with strictly monotonic continuous corruption functions
unmapped: Learner never observes the reward; it observes a Bernoulli feedback whose mean is g_a(mu_a) for a known, arm-dependent, strictly monotonic continuous mean-corruption function g_a
Learner knows the corruption functions g_a
settings.definition_quote: If the learner pulls an arm a at time t, they receive a reward R_t drawn from the distribution nu_a with mean mu_a and observe a feedback F_t drawn from the distribution varsigma_a with mean lambda_a. We assume that, for each arm, there exists a loose link between the reward and the feedback through a known mean-corruption function g_a ... g_a(mu_a)=lambda_a

settings.name_in_paper: Bernoulli corrupt bandit with continuous corruption functions (lower bound)
unmapped: Learner observes only corrupted Bernoulli feedback with mean g_a(mu_a), g_a known and continuous
settings.definition_quote: Given continuous corruption functions {g_a}, any uniformly efficient algorithm for a Bernoulli corrupt bandit problem satisfies ...

unmapped: Feedback is the reward passed through a known randomized-response channel with matrix M_a (p00(a), p11(a))
settings.definition_quote: Randomized response can be simulated by a Bernoulli corrupt bandit and the corresponding corruption scheme can be encoded by the matrix M_a ... g_a(x) = 1 - p00(a) + [p00(a)+p11(a)-1] x.

settings.name_in_paper: Bernoulli bandit with epsilon-locally differentially private feedback corruption scheme
unmapped: Local differential privacy via randomized response with p00=p11=e^eps/(1+e^eps)
settings.definition_quote: A bandit feedback corruption scheme g is epsilon-locally differentially private for epsilon >= 0 if for all reward sequences ... P[g(R) in S] <= e^epsilon P[g(R') in S].

symbols.D_i: Bernoulli KL d(lambda_i, g_i(mu_star)) between arm i's mean feedback and the image of the optimal mean under g_i

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: Given continuous corruption functions $\{g_a\}_{a \in A}$, any uniformly efficient algorithm for a Bernoulli corrupt bandit problem satisfies, $$\liminf_{T\rightarrow \infty}\frac{\cRegret_T}{\log(T)} \geq \sum_{a = 2}^{K} \frac{\Delta_a}{d\left(\lambda_a,g_a(\mu_1)\right)}.$$

results.notes: Uniformly efficient: regret o(T^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1) on every instance.

symbols.C_rem: instance-dependent constant hidden in the O(sqrt(log T)) term

conditions: corruption functions g_a strictly monotonic and continuous

source.label: UB_KLUCB_Theorem
source.quote: \KLUCBCF \ using  $f(t) \defined \log(t)+3\log(\log(t))$ on a $K$-armed Bernoulli corrupt bandit with strictly monotonic and continuous corruption functions $\{g_a\}_{a \in A}$ satisfies at time $T$, \Regret_T \leq \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{\Delta_a \log (T) }{d\left(\lambda_a,g_a(\mu_1)\right)}  + O(\sqrt{\log(T)}).

results.notes: Second-order O(sqrt(log T)) term represented by C_rem. Appendix gives explicit finite-time bound with sqrt(2 pi) (D'_a^2/D_a^3)^{1/2} sqrt(log T + 3 log log T) + (4e + 3/D_a) log log T + 2(D'_a/D_a)^2 + 4 per arm. Algorithm lists T as parameter but index uses only f(t), so treated as anytime.

symbols.g_i_mu_star: g_i(mu_star), image of the optimal mean reward under arm i's corruption function

conditions: corruption functions g_a strictly monotonic and continuous

source.label: UB_UCB_Theorem
source.quote: With $f(t) \defined \log(t)+3\log(\log(t))$, the regret of \textsc{UCB-CF} at time $T$ on a $K$-armed Bernoulli corrupt bandit with strictly monotonic and continuous corruption functions $\{g_a\}_{a \in A}$ is in $O\Big( \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{ \Delta_a \log(T)}{ (\lambda_a - g_a(\mu_1))^2 } \Big)$.

symbols.C_psi: constant depending on psi, the means and the corruption functions

conditions: corruption functions g_a strictly monotonic and continuous

source.label: UB_TSCF_Theorem
source.quote: When \TSCF \ is run on a $K$-armed Bernoulli corrupt bandit with strictly monotonic and continuous corruption functions $\{g_a\}_{a \in A}$, for all $\psi >0$, there exists a constant $C_\psi \defined C(\psi,\{\mu_a\}_{a \in A},\{g_a\}_{a \in A})$ such that at time $T$, \[\cRegret_T \leq (1+\psi)\sum_{a = 2}^K\frac{\Delta_a\log(T)}{d(\lambda_a,g_a(\mu_1))} + C_\psi.\]

results.notes: psi plays role of eps_alg. TS-CF does not use T.

symbols.p_00_i: randomized-response probability p00(i) for arm i
symbols.p_11_i: randomized-response probability p11(i) for arm i
symbols.C_rem: instance-dependent constant in the O(sqrt(log T)) term

source.label: UB_corollary
source.quote: The regret of \KLUCBCF \ and \TSCF \ for a $K$-armed Bernoulli MAB problem with randomized response using corruption matrices $\{\mathbb{M}\}_{a \in A}$ at time $T$ is $$ \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{2\log(T)}{ \Delta_a (p_{00}(a) + p_{11}(a) -1)^2 } + O(\sqrt{\log{(T)}} ).$$

results.notes: Stated as 'is' (interpreted as upper bound via Pinsker). The constant 2 in the numerator is as printed; Pinsker would give 1/2. Recorded as stated.

symbols.p_00_i: randomized-response probability p00(i) for arm i
symbols.p_11_i: randomized-response probability p11(i) for arm i
symbols.C_rem: instance-dependent constant in the O(sqrt(log T)) term

source.label: UB_corollary
source.quote: The regret of \KLUCBCF \ and \TSCF \ for a $K$-armed Bernoulli MAB problem with randomized response using corruption matrices $\{\mathbb{M}\}_{a \in A}$ at time $T$ is $$ \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{2\log(T)}{ \Delta_a (p_{00}(a) + p_{11}(a) -1)^2 } + O(\sqrt{\log{(T)}} ).$$

results.notes: For TS-CF, Theorem 3 only gives (1+psi) factor plus constant, so the O(sqrt(log T)) remainder does not directly follow; recorded as stated.

symbols.C_rem: instance-dependent constant in the O(sqrt(log T)) term

conditions: corruption via randomized response with p00=p11=e^eps/(1+e^eps)

source.label: DPUB_corollary
source.quote: The regret of \KLUCBCF \ or \TSCF \ at time $T$ with $\epsilon$-locally differentially private bandit feedback corruption scheme is $$ \cRegret_T \leq \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{2\log(T)}{ \Delta_a \big( \frac{e^\epsilon - 1}{e^\epsilon + 1}\big)^2} + O(\sqrt{\log{(T)}} ).$$

results.notes: Specialisation of Corollary 2 with the optimal LDP randomized-response matrix.

symbols.C_rem: instance-dependent constant in the O(sqrt(log T)) term

conditions: corruption via randomized response with p00=p11=e^eps/(1+e^eps)

source.label: DPUB_corollary
source.quote: The regret of \KLUCBCF \ or \TSCF \ at time $T$ with $\epsilon$-locally differentially private bandit feedback corruption scheme is $$ \cRegret_T \leq \sum_{a = 2}^{K}\frac{2\log(T)}{ \Delta_a \big( \frac{e^\epsilon - 1}{e^\epsilon + 1}\big)^2} + O(\sqrt{\log{(T)}} ).$$

results.notes: As for r6, the O(sqrt(log T)) remainder for TS-CF is not directly implied by Theorem 3; recorded as stated.
